scope: Fresh independently seeded Debian disks in the Intel dual-guest composition
host: madmax, Intel i9-14900KF, Linux KVM with nested VMX

provisioning.result: Both full raw disks generated with exact seed readback and complete root-region verification. Initial compiler failure from /tmp quota retained; retry using TMPDIR under /var/tmp succeeded.

observations: Initial secondary CREATE returned not-ready; primary CREATE then succeeded with handle 1 and secondary retry with handle 2.
Both guest kernels booted and mounted their ext4 root filesystems.
Primary entered emergency mode after timeout waiting for the EFI partition device and failed boot-efi.mount dependency.
Secondary systemd reported Failed to fork off sandboxing environment for executing generators: Protocol error, then froze execution at guest time 189.486164.
Source GPT partition IDs match source fstab. Earlier already-provisioned primary guest has the same fstab, the expected /dev/disk/by-partuuid links, and mounted /boot/efi.
Host load average was 36.64, 20.65, 15.58 during investigation; causal significance is not established.

evidence.contents: Console snapshots, QEMU log and arguments, guest list, seed logs including quota failure, initial disk hashes, OS image hash, host load. No private keys or guest disks.

limits: No independent SSH or persistent storage acceptance. Earlier two-guest login proof used already-provisioned baseline copies and does not prove fresh concurrent provisioning. QEMU 1385114 and its disks retained for diagnosis; earlier QEMU 1292940 preserved. Root cause remains unconfirmed.
